summary: Todd Gibson is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Indiana University, earning his PhD attested in 1991, under the instruction of György Kara.

Todd Thornton Lewis works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under mentors including Ainslie T. Embree, Morton Klass, Alex Wayman, Margaret Mead, and Theodore Riccardi. He held professorships at the College of the Holy Cross.

Tokan Tada was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Akita High School and long-term at Sera Monastery (1913–1923). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1924), Tohoku University (1925), and Toyo Bunko (1956).
Toke Lindegaard Knudsen studied under Kim Plofker around 2004 to 2008 and under David Pingree in 2008.

Tokio Takata specializes in Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University and the EHESS. His career includes posts at Otaru University of Commerce (1981–1983), Kyoto University (1983–2014), and Fudan University (2016–2022).

Tokugen Sakai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University, and under Kodo Sawaki. He held positions at Komazawa University (1949–1987) and Eihei-ji (1977–1987).

Tokuno Oda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara and Junjirō Takakusu. He taught at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Fukui Chugakko, and Toyo University.

Tokuryu Yamauchi was a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University under Kitarō Nishida and at the University of Freiburg under Edmund Husserl and Martin Heidegger. He held professorships at Hitotsubashi, Kyoto, and Ryukoku universities.

Tom Tillemans works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Jacques May (~1978–1989) and served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Lausanne (attested 1987–2018) and Visiting Numata Chair at the University of Calgary.

Tomoko Masuzawa specializes in religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at International Christian University, Yale University, and UC Santa Barbara (PhD 1985). She held faculty appointments at UNC Chapel Hill (~1987–2002) and the University of Michigan (from 1999).
Tomoyasu Oshima is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under Toshifumi Goto and served as a part-time lecturer at Kyoto University (attested 2012).
Tomoyuki Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University and served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).
Tomoyuki Uno is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who was a JSPS special researcher (attested 1998) and an associate professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2000–2006).

Tomy Augustine is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned a master's at the University of Madras and a PhD at Banaras Hindu University, studying under Munni K. Agrawal and C. S. Sundaram. He held a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

Toni Huber specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Canterbury (1993), studying under Jim Wilson, Paul Harrison, and William Sax. He held professorships at Victoria University of Wellington and the University of Berlin.

Tony K. Stewart is an Indologist and scholar of religion who studied at Western Kentucky University (~1972–1976). He held posts in philosophy and religion at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and Vanderbilt University (~2011).

Torakazu Doi was a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe (~1923–1926). He later held posts at Sagami Women's University and Dokkyo University (~1964–1971).

Torkel Brekke works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Oslo and the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich. He has held professorships at Oslo Metropolitan University and MF Norwegian School of Theology, Religion and Society.

Torsten Wiesel studied at the Karolinska Institute (~1947–1954). He held academic posts at Johns Hopkins University (~1955–1959), Harvard University (~1959–1983), and Rockefeller University (1983–1998).

Toru Haneda specialized in Sinology, history, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, later serving as professor, dean, and director at Kyoto University, as well as head of the Institute of Eastern Culture.
